headline: Crude gapped down on the Sunday reopen, WTI losing 6.7 percent to 93.62 dollars and Brent 6.6 percent to 97.00 dollars, wiping out the entire spike that followed the 11 September strike on Saudi Arabia's East West pipeline.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,650.50, up 0.17 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.39 percent to 26,522.55, while the Dow slipped 0.18 percent to 51,682.64 and the 10 year Treasury yield ended at 4.998 percent after touching its highest level since 2007 earlier in the week. The moves followed the Federal Reserve's 25 basis point hike on 16 September to 3.75 to 4 percent, after which CME FedWatch odds of another increase in October rose to about 58 percent from 42 percent a week earlier.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 rose 0.33 percent on Friday to 23,346.40 and Bank Nifty gained 0.54 percent to 56,358.70, but both benchmarks logged a sixth consecutive weekly loss, the longest run since 2020, with the Sensex ending at 74,294.96. FIIs bought a net 599.50 crore rupees and DIIs a net 1,019.70 crore rupees in the cash segment, India VIX fell 7.3 percent to 11.39, the rupee sits at 95.86 per dollar, and over the weekend Tata Trusts called N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons chairman void and questioned the casting vote used to carry it.
summary.global: Asia closed higher on Friday, with the Nikkei 225 up 1.38 percent to 65,018.95 after the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25 percent on a 7 to 2 vote that sent the yen past 156 per dollar, and the Hang Seng up 0.60 percent to 24,750.78 as the Hang Seng Tech Index added 2.2 percent. Europe went the other way as the STOXX 600 fell 1.1 percent to 635.45, the FTSE 100 lost 1.45 percent to 10,659.10 and the DAX 1.6 percent to 25,304.06, with autos down 3.4 percent after Volkswagen cut its outlook and flagged 10 billion euros of one off items.

calendar.what: Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee speaks and the Chicago Fed National Activity Index is released, opening a week with about ten Fed speaker appearances. The NSE and Sonaselection India IPOs close. India publishes eight core industries data.

Richmond Fed manufacturing index for September. AutoZone reports fourth quarter results before the US open. The Varmora Granito IPO opens in India at 140 to 148 rupees. The Avalanche Helicon mainnet upgrade activates at 11:00 US Eastern.

S&P Global flash US manufacturing and services PMIs for September, plus the US current account. Swastika Infra, ArMee Infotech, Elevate Campuses and Adroit Industries IPOs open in India. Bamboo Insurance and Amaero are set to price in the US.

Costco reports fourth quarter fiscal 2026 results after the US close, the week's most watched release. MBA mortgage applications and US new home sales. The A-One Steels India IPO opens. BW Industrial Holdings and Web3Labs Global are on the US pricing calendar.

US initial jobless claims, durable goods orders and the final reading of second quarter GDP. The Swastika Infra, ArMee Infotech, Elevate Campuses and Adroit Industries IPOs close in India. SBI meets institutional investors virtually through a Citi group meeting.
No scheduled market events. Markets are closed for the weekend.

No scheduled market events. The August US PCE price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, together with personal income and spending, follows on 27 or 28 September depending on the release calendar.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to central banks. The Federal Reserve raised rates a quarter point on 16 September to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike since 2023, and the Bank of Japan followed on 18 September with a split 7 to 2 vote that lifted its policy rate to a 31 year high of 1.25 percent, yet the yen weakened past 156 per dollar because two board members dissented and Governor Ueda made no commitment to further moves. US equities finished mixed as the 10 year Treasury yield came back to about 5 percent after touching a 19 year high above 5.04 percent ahead of the Fed, with the Dow down 1.69 percent on the week while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.72 percent. India was the weak spot, where the Nifty and Sensex logged a sixth consecutive weekly decline, the longest losing run in six years, under crude above 100 dollars, tighter global policy and a deepening Tata Sons governance dispute. Metals held their ground, with copper up about 2 percent on the week as the Yangshan import premium climbed 72 percent in September to a near four year high and silver adding 3.46 percent, while crypto turned sharply higher into the weekend on post Fed relief and rotation into altcoins. Next week brings S&P Global flash PMIs on 23 September, a heavy run of Fed speakers, Costco and Nike earnings on 24 September, and in India the Varmora Granito, Elevate Campuses, ArMee Infotech and A-One Steels offers alongside the close of the NSE IPO on 21 September.
